title: Restriction of the strict-limit completed open exchange and its units
statement:
Fix the finite-field datum $k=\overline{\mathbf F}_q$, a prime $\ell\ne\operatorname{char}k$, a finite extension $E/\mathbf Q_\ell$, its valuation ring $R=\mathcal O_E$, a uniformizer $t$, and $A_n=R/t^n$ for $n\ge1$ [def-weil-finite-field-fiber, def-weil-l-adic-coefficient-extension]. On each small pro-etale site put $B_W=\lim_n(A_n)_W$ [def-weil-pbc-proetale-site, def-weil-completed-integral-coefficients] and use the ordinary unbounded module derived category $D(B_W)$ [def-weil-sheaf-of-modules-category, def-weil-abstract-derived-category]. Open extension and restriction mean exact ringed-slice functors $e_!\dashv e^*$, applied termwise [lem-pur-site-restriction-module-adjunction-exact].
Let $U'\xrightarrow a U$, $j':U'\hookrightarrow X'$, $j:U\hookrightarrow X$, $h:X'\to X$ be a Cartesian square of finite-type $k$-schemes with $j$ open [def-cbc-open-immersion-square, def-weil-scheme-morphism-properties], and let $K\in D(B_U)$ be derived complete in the Roos-triangle sense [def-weil-derived-complete]. For $H\in D(B_W)$ write $H_n=H\otimes^L_{B_W}(A_n)_W$ and $Q_W(H)_\bullet=(\operatorname{Res}_n H_n)_n$, with the strict quotient transitions; $\operatorname{Res}_n$ forgets to $B_W$-modules along $B_W\to(A_n)_W$ [def-weil-integral-reduction-tower]. Use flat-term K-flat representatives [def-pc-kflat-complex, def-pc-flat-sheaf-modules, lem-pc-kflat-resolution], the total right derived inverse limit on strict towers, and its normalized Roos model and augmentation comparison [lem-cbc-exact-product-functor-strict-limit].
Use the completed pullbacks $Lh^*_{\mathrm{comp}},La^*_{\mathrm{comp}}$ [def-weil-pbc-completed-pullback]. Let $F_h,F_a$ denote the simultaneous finite constant-coefficient pullbacks on strict quotient towers, and let $b_\bullet:F_hJQ_U(K)_\bullet\xrightarrow{\sim}J'F_aQ_U(K)_\bullet$ be the finite open exchanges of [lem-cbc-finite-open-exchange-scalars], with $J,J'$ termwise extension. Its inverse is the simultaneous inverse-open-unit transpose. Identify the reduction tower of $j_!K$ with $JQ_U(K)_\bullet$ by the canonical open scalar map [lem-sf-integral-open-reduction-comparison]. Let $\lambda_{j'}:j'_!R\lim F_aQ_U(K)_\bullet\xrightarrow{\sim}R\lim J'F_aQ_U(K)_\bullet$ be the augmentation-normalized exact-product Roos comparison [lem-cbc-exact-product-functor-strict-limit].
Under these fixed strict reduction identifications, the specified completed exchange of [lem-cbc-completed-extension-zero-comparison] is exactly
$$\Beta_K=\lambda_{j'}^{-1}\circ R\lim(b_\bullet):Lh^*_{\mathrm{comp}}j_!K\xrightarrow{\sim}j'_!La^*_{\mathrm{comp}}K.$$
Both endpoints are complete. The finite pullback compositors [lem-weil-pbc-proetale-derived-pullback-composition], followed by functorial strict derived limit, give a canonical isomorphism $\Theta_K:j'^*Lh^*_{\mathrm{comp}}j_!K\xrightarrow{\sim}La^*_{\mathrm{comp}}K$, with the open unit used to identify $j^*j_!K=K$. Under the open unit $j'^*j'_!=1$,
$$j'^*\Beta_K=\Theta_K.$$
The comparison $j'^*Lh^*_{\mathrm{comp}}\cong La^*_{\mathrm{comp}}j^*$ used in $\Theta$ carries the restricted ordinary-to-completed pullback unit to the corresponding unit after ordinary pullback composition [def-sf-pull-completion-comparison]. On simultaneous strict systems, restriction of $b_\bullet$ is the identity after the finite pullback-composition and open-unit identifications. Restriction of $\lambda_{j'}$ is the identity comparison: its product comparison is the identity on every projection and its Roos map is that same identity on both signed summands. These equalities include the augmentations and their completion units. Thus the displayed equality is one of actual completed morphisms, not a consequence of assumed faithfulness of separate finite-reduction evaluations.

proof.text: Apply [lem-sf-open-roos-unit-adjunction] to the open immersions $j,j'$. Its finite-type hypotheses are exactly those here: the schemes are Noetherian and qcqs, both opens are quasi-compact, $(R,(t))$ is an admissible adic datum, and the coefficient restriction isomorphisms preserve every quotient projection. The same statement identifies the assumed Roos-triangle completeness of $K$ with intrinsic completeness and invertibility of its actual quotient-augmentation unit. We may therefore apply lemmas stated for intrinsic completeness, without replacing the augmentation by an arbitrary isomorphism. Write $L_W=R\lim$ on strict $B_W$-towers and $\mathsf H$ for its normalized signed Roos model.

source.place: Tags 099N, lemma-pushforward-Noetherian-case (2),(5), and 09BN, lemma-open-immersion; admissibility and actual-unit bridge supplied by the cited node.

proof.text: The module categories on all four sites have exact countable products by [lem-weil-proetale-countable-products-exact]. The functors $j'_!$ and $j'^*$ are additive and exact by [lem-pur-site-restriction-module-adjunction-exact]. The former preserves countable products by [lem-cbc-ringed-open-extension-products], since $j'$ is quasi-compact; the latter does so by [lem-weil-pbc-right-adjoint-preserves-limits], applied to $j'_!\dashv j'^*$ and the small discrete countable index category. Thus [lem-cbc-exact-product-functor-strict-limit] applies separately to both functors. Denote its normalized restriction comparison by $\rho_T:j'^*L_{X'}T\xrightarrow{\sim}L_{U'}j'^*T$ and its extension comparison by $\lambda_M:j'_!L_{U'}M\xrightarrow{\sim}L_{X'}J'M$. Both comparisons preserve strict augmentations. No product-preservation assertion is required of $F_h$ or $F_a$.

source.place: Tag 09BP, lemma-j-shriek-limits; normalized exact-product comparisons and the augmentation clause of the cited strict-limit node.

proof.text: Choose a flat-term K-flat representative $P$ of $K$ using [lem-pc-kflat-resolution]. By [lem-cbc-ringed-open-flat-resolution], $j_!P$ is again flat-term K-flat, so it computes the reductions of $j_!K$. Put $T=Q_U(K)_\bullet$ and $M=F_aT$. The canonical isomorphism $r_j$ of [lem-sf-integral-open-reduction-comparison] identifies the entire reduction system of $j_!K$ with $JT$, including quotient transitions, and gives completeness of $j_!K$. The simultaneous comparison of [lem-cbc-completed-ring-strict-finite-exchange] identifies pullback of this system with $F_hJT$ and identifies its exchange with the strict finite map $b:T_h=F_hJT\to J'M$. These are maps of systems over $B_{X'}$ through its quotient projections, not selected maps between separate derived evaluations.

source.place: Tag 099N, lemma-pushforward-Noetherian-case (5); strict finite exchange and open reduction interfaces of the cited nodes.

proof.text: At each finite constant coefficient $A_n$, let $\alpha_n:j'^*h_n^*j_!P_n\to a_n^*P_n$ be pullback composition followed by the inverse open unit. The compositor is the one normalized on representatives in [lem-weil-pbc-proetale-derived-pullback-composition]; its coefficient-isomorphism hypotheses hold here for finite constant sheaves. By [lem-sf-open-tensor-normalization] the open units identify sections with themselves. Let $u'_n:N_n\to j'^*j'_!N_n$, $N_n=a_n^*P_n$, and let $d_n=b_n^{-1}$. The inverse-mate formula of [lem-cbc-finite-open-exchange-scalars] says precisely $j'^*d_n\circ u'_n=\alpha_n^{-1}$, by the definition of adjunct. Inverting gives $(u'_n)^{-1}\circ j'^*b_n=\alpha_n$. The same cited statement makes $b_n,d_n$, their units, and composition identifications compatible with every quotient transition. We obtain an equality of strict tower maps $(u'_M)^{-1}\circ j'^*b=\alpha:j'^*T_h\to M$, with $u'$ the termwise open unit. In the specified composition and unit coordinates this is the identity on the simultaneous system.

source.place: Tags 09BN, lemma-open-immersion, and 099N; finite-composition input: sites-cohomology.tex Tag 0D6D, lemma-derived-pullback-composition.

proof.text: The definition [def-weil-pbc-completed-pullback] now represents $Lh^*_{\mathrm{comp}}j_!K$ by $L_{X'}T_h$ and $La^*_{\mathrm{comp}}K$ by $L_{U'}M$. The canonical map of [lem-cbc-completed-extension-zero-comparison] is defined from the finite exchanges and the extension/derived-limit comparison. Use the augmentation-normalized comparison of step 2 for that latter comparison: [lem-cbc-exact-product-functor-strict-limit] identifies it with $\lambda_M$, including the comparison obtained by resolving the image tower. Hence, in the fixed strict reduction coordinates, the specified exchange is exactly $\Beta_K=\lambda_M^{-1}\circ L_{X'}(b)$. Both factors are invertible. The completed-extension comparison also states that both endpoints are intrinsically complete. The equivalence in step 1 converts this to the completeness predicate of the item.

source.place: Tag 099N, lemma-pushforward-Noetherian-case (2),(5); the canonical-map clause of the cited completed open comparison.

proof.text:
Compute the restriction of $\lambda_M$. In the section-normalized open-unit coordinates, the product comparison for $j'_!$, after applying $j'^*$ and its product comparison, has $n$-th projection $\operatorname{pr}_n$: this follows from its defining equation $\operatorname{pr}_n\phi=j'_!(\operatorname{pr}_n)$ and naturality of the open unit. Equality into a product is equality of its projections, so this composite product comparison is the identity. In the signed model $\mathsf H(M)^q=(\prod M_n)^q\oplus(\prod M_n)^{q-1}$, the corresponding map is therefore $(x,y)\mapsto(x,y)$. It commutes with $d(x,y)=(dx,(1-s)x-dy)$ since the open-unit identification commutes with all transitions. The conjugation formula for $\lambda$ in [lem-cbc-exact-product-functor-strict-limit] and the same normalization for $\rho$ give
$$L_{U'}((u'_M)^{-1})\circ\rho_{J'M}\circ j'^*(\lambda_M)\circ u'_{L_{U'}M}=1.$$
Here $u'$ is the section-normalized open unit of [lem-sf-open-tensor-normalization]. The augmentation is $(\gamma,0)$ in [lem-weil-strict-roos-comparison], so the very same identity fixes it. There is no undetermined cone map or sign in the second summand.

source.place: Tags 09BN and 09BP; signed Roos normalization: sites-cohomology.tex Tag 0941, lemma-derived-limit-is-ok; explicit identity calculation from the cited comparisons.

proof.text:
Naturality of $\rho$ for the strict map $b:T_h\to J'M$ gives
$$\rho_{J'M}\circ j'^*L_{X'}(b)=L_{U'}(j'^*b)\circ\rho_{T_h}.$$
This is also immediate in [lem-weil-strict-roos-comparison]: both sides apply the same product map of $b$ on both signed coordinates. Substitute step 5 into $j'^*\Beta_K$, then use the equation in step 6 to obtain
$$ (u'_{L_{U'}M})^{-1}\circ j'^*\Beta_K
 =L_{U'}((u'_M)^{-1}\circ j'^*b)\circ\rho_{T_h}
 =L_{U'}(\alpha)\circ\rho_{T_h}.$$
The last equality is step 4. The right side is exactly $\Theta_K$: it first commutes open restriction with the normalized strict limit and then applies the finite pullback compositors and the open unit. Thus $j'^*\Beta_K=\Theta_K$ under the stated endpoint identification. The equality is obtained on simultaneous Roos maps and hence holds in the ambient completed-coefficient derived category.

source.place: Tag 099N, lemma-pushforward-Noetherian-case (5); normalized strict-limit naturality and the explicit calculation of steps 4–6.

proof.text: Check the ordinary-to-completed units before taking limits. For a complete $H\in D(B_X)$, choose a flat-term K-flat $P\to H$. Ringed pullback and restriction preserve these representatives by [lem-weil-pbc-ringed-topoi-derived-tensor-pullback]. Write $\delta_H:j'^*Lh^*H\xrightarrow{\sim}La^*j^*H$ for the ordinary ringed-square compositor specified in [lem-sf-open-tensor-normalization]. The strict reduction comparison for restriction in [lem-sf-immersion-completed-pullback-comparison] identifies $j'^*F_hQ_X(H)$ with $F_aQ_U(j^*H)$. Under this identification the two strict augmentations agree after $\delta_H$: both send a local pullback tensor $r'\otimes p$ to $r'_n\otimes(p\otimes1)$ at level $n$. Restriction simply views this section over the open; the constant-section compositor and open unit do not change it. This equation is balanced, respects differentials degreewise, and commutes with $A_{n+1}\to A_n$ because $r'_{n+1}$ reduces to $r'_n$. The completed structural maps used on the two sides have equal $n$-th projections, namely restriction of the same constant-section map. Thus they agree as maps into $B_{U'}$; [lem-cbc-adic-pullback-presentation-transport] carries these coefficient identifications, their strict augmentations, and the derived representative comparisons to the specified constructions. This does not assume that $h^{-1}B_X\to B_{X'}$ is invertible.

source.place: Tag 099N, lemma-pushforward-Noetherian-case (2),(5); sites-cohomology.tex Tag 0D6D; explicit tensor-generator and quotient-projection calculation.

proof.text:
Let $v_h:Lh^*H\to Lh^*_{\mathrm{comp}}H$ and $v_a:La^*j^*H\to La^*_{\mathrm{comp}}j^*H$ be the actual units of [def-weil-pbc-completed-pullback]. They are induced by the strict augmentations of step 8. Let $c_H:j'^*Lh^*_{\mathrm{comp}}H\to La^*_{\mathrm{comp}}j^*H$ be $\rho$ followed by the strict finite-composition/restriction comparison. By [lem-weil-strict-roos-comparison], the two augmented maps are represented by $(\gamma,0)$. Step 8 makes their first components equal, and their second components are both zero; the augmentation clause of [lem-cbc-exact-product-functor-strict-limit] therefore gives the actual equation
$$c_H\circ j'^*v_h=v_a\circ\delta_H.$$
This is precisely the normalization retained in [def-sf-pull-completion-comparison], whose ordinary-to-completed map uses the recorded quotient unit. Apply it to $H=j_!K$ and identify $j^*j_!K=K$ with its specified open unit: the $c_H$ used here is the comparison in $\Theta_K$. Together with the augmentation identity in step 6 this proves all asserted completion-unit compatibilities. Functoriality of the strict maps and the normalized comparisons gives naturality in $K$.
